ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the Vanuatu Consolidated Sanctions List administered by VFSC, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and Interpol Red Notices. Enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) pursuant to section 22 of the AML/CFT Act 2011, including source of wealth, source of funds, and senior management approval. Ongoing transaction monitoring and risk-based periodic review are required under section 21 and the AML/CFT Regulation 2017.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Online Company Search and Name Reservation Portal (vufsc.vu / in-person filing through licensed registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be in English or French; names must use Latin script. If a non-Latin script trade name is used, a statutory English transliteration is mandatory on the application. Name must end with a suffix indicating limited liability: 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or corresponding abbreviation. For International Companies, the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing Vanuatu company, international company, overseas company registered in Vanuatu, or reserved name. A foreign-language name is permitted where it is a transliteration using Latin characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal to the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission Registry within 14 business days, stating the grounds of objection, attaching the name reservation receipt, and, if applicable, a legal opinion on distinctiveness. The VFSC Name Approval Panel issues a determination within 10 business days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Vanuatu Supreme Court within 21 days. A successful appeal grants a fresh reservation period of 30 days. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a new reservation with a revised name subject to a new filing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office for an International Company. Section 8 of the International Companies Act 1992 requires a physical registered office in Vanuatu maintained by a licensed registered agent, with physical access by VFSC and service of process. A virtual mail-forwarding address may be used strictly as a business correspondence address in addition to the physical registered office. For a no-code website builder business (ISIC 6201), the VFSC accepts a foreign operational address as principal place of business, but the statutory registered office must remain physical in Vanuatu.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate. The VFSC conducts risk-based random inspections. For a standard low-risk no-code software activity without statutory licensing, the probability of unannounced physical inspection is approximately 5-10% annually. If the company receives payments via Stripe or Paddle, the VFSC and Financial Intelligence Unit monitor banking and payment reports and may commission a targeted inspection in the event of suspicious transaction reports (STRs). The registered agent must maintain the registered office open during ordinary business hours and is subject to inspection compliance checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act No. 32 of 1992, as consolidated (Cap. 222); ss. 6 (registration by application), 7 (memorandum and articles), 10 (registered office), 14 (shares and no minimum capital requirement)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - International Companies Registry Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of an International Company together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or capital deposit account is required for an International Company; shares may be issued for par value, no par value, or nominal consideration as determined by the board.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTIONS OF [●] INTERNATIONAL COMPANY, adopted by the founding director(s) on [●], pursuant to the Memorandum and Articles of Association.

RESOLVED, that the subscription of the founding shareholder for [●] ordinary shares is accepted, shares are allotted as fully paid, and the share register is opened accordingly.

RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be established at the office of [●] Registered Agent, Port Vila, Vanuatu, and the Registered Agent is authorized to maintain statutory registers, custody of books, and service of process.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [●] be appointed director and [●] company secretary, with full authority to execute governmental filings, open bank accounts, and conduct ordinary business.

These resolutions are effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC International Companies Registry (via licensed Registered Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through a licensed Registered Agent. Avoid names prohibited under section 15 of the International Companies Act, including words implying banking, trust, insurance, or regulated financial activity unless a VFSC licence is held. The Registry reserves the approved name for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of proposed shareholder or beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or prohibited words, the Registered Agent immediately files an alternate name; the reservation fee is not refunded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Vanuatu Registered Agent acting under VFSC supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with the International Companies Act. Each founding subscriber must execute the instrument before the Registered Agent or a notary public. The instrument must state the authorised share capital and governance provisions agreed by the founding shareholder.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as Registered Agent
Certified copy of passport of each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution or notarisation is defective, the Registered Agent corrects the execution block and obtains re-signature while preserving the original intended incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC International Companies Registry, Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed Registered Agent submits the Application for Registration, the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, consents, and the VFSC filing fee of USD 300. The applicant receives a VFSC receipt and control number acknowledging the filing.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of an International Company
Payment confirmation of official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC issues a query or objection, the Registered Agent responds within 14 calendar days with amended pages or a supplementary affidavit; failure to respond results in deemed withdrawal and restart of the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon VFSC approval, the Registered Agent collects the Certificate of Incorporation. The Company verifies its legal name, registration number, incorporation date, and issued share capital as recorded in the certificate and statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Approved Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical errors, the Registered Agent files a rectification request with VFSC; correction is issued without re-application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Board Resolutions and Establish Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board with assistance of Licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene or pass the First Board Resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. Issue share certificates, deliver statutory registers, seal, and corporate books to the registered office. Where commercial payment operations require a USD account, the board opens a corporate bank account with a Vanuatu licensed bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional due diligence, the Registered Agent provides certified corporate documents and a business profile for the company to satisfy KYC requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial licensing regime applies to a pure digital service business classified under ISIC 6201
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - statutory licence exemption under the Vanuatu International Companies Act for non-financial services activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 - Exempt; no EIA registration required for cloud-based software development and no-code website building
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, or hazardous industrial waste are generated. Where office e-waste is generated, storage, transport, and recycling must comply with Vanuatu Waste Management and Pollution Control standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety or structural clearance is statutorily mandated for a digital services business. If a physical office is leased, the lessee must obtain a certificate of occupancy and basic fire extinguisher inspection from the relevant municipal authority; occupational health and safety registration is recommended where employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Department of Customs and Inland Revenue, Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, Port Vila, Vanuatu; administrative portal administered by the Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Service (VCIR) via the official government e-services gateway.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Vanuatu International Companies (ICs) are tax-exempt and are not ordinarily required to obtain a domestic VAT or income tax identification number. If a physical customs or employer registration need arises, a foreign entity must file a written application with the VCIR using the prescribed registration form, accompanied by: (i) certificate of incorporation and IC registration certificate issued by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC); (ii) copy of the registered office address certificate issued by a licensed registered agent; (iii) particulars of directors and shareholders; (iv) beneficial ownership declaration; and (v) a statement confirming the intended activities in Vanuatu. Processing is typically completed within 5–10 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election exists under Vanuatu law because Vanuatu does not impose income tax. The International Company may statutorily elect to remain a non-resident exempt entity under the International Companies Act [CAP 222], which serves as the de facto exemption election. Hybrid mismatch rules under BEPS Action 2 have not been enacted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 3,000,000 Vatu of taxable supplies per annum for resident businesses; not applicable to International Companies, which fall outside the chargeable scope of Vanuatu VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Vanuatu has no real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no e-invoicing API requirement, and no digital stamping for standard invoices. Registered VAT suppliers must issue paper or electronic tax invoices containing the prescribed VAT Act fields and retain them for at least 10 years. Customs export declarations are processed electronically through the ASYCUDA World customs platform; exempt International Companies serving offshore clients are outside the VAT invoicing and clearance regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAT Act, exports of goods are zero-rated when the goods are physically exported from Vanuatu within the applicable time limit and the exporter retains prescribed evidence of export. Services are zero-rated if supplied to a recipient outside Vanuatu, enjoyed wholly outside Vanuatu, or supplied directly in connection with goods situated outside Vanuatu. A Vanuatu International Company providing software-as-a-service or website-builder tools to non-residents is outside the charge to VAT and is not eligible for input VAT refunds; a resident VAT-registered vendor seeking zero-rating must satisfy the documentary export bundle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World electronic export entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from Vanuatu
Bank inward remittance certificate or SWIFT payment receipt evidencing receipt of foreign currency proceeds
Contemporaneous contract or purchase order showing delivery to a non-resident
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective assessment by the Comptroller of Customs and Inland Revenue: the unpaid VAT becomes immediately due together with interest at the statutory rate, and a civil penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded may be imposed. In cases of deliberate fraud, criminal prosecution may result in a fine of up to VT 5,000,000 and/or imprisonment for up to five years. The Comptroller may extend the assessment period to eight years in fraud or wilful default cases and four years in ordinary cases. An International Company that improperly holds itself out as VAT-exempt for domestic supplies remains personally liable for VAT, customs duties, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV), acting as the monetary authority, national regulator of licensed credit institutions, and operator of the Vanuatu National Payment System.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations. The vatu is freely convertible for all current international transactions, and profit remittance is unrestricted for International Companies engaged in offshore software services, subject to standard bank documentation (audited financial statements, tax clearance from the Vanuatu Customs & Inland Revenue Department, and, if applicable, the Vanuatu Investment Promotion Agency (VIPA) certificate for foreign investors). Capital-account inflows require notification or approval under the Foreign Investment Act 1998 via VIPA; no exchange-control licensing or repatriation quotas apply. Material FX consideration: the vatu is officially pegged to the Australian dollar at approximately 1 VUV = 0.01 AUD, creating structural currency risk for USD-denominated SaaS subscription revenue that should be managed through treasury hedging.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio exist under RBV rules. Export receipts for software, licensing, and SaaS services may be retained indefinitely in foreign-currency accounts (USD/EUR/AUD) at licensed commercial banks, subject only to bank-level AML/CFT activity monitoring and ongoing economic-substance evidence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Vanuatu Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Trade Settlement Account
Operational Account (retail-oriented; less suited to offshore International Company treasury)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with a structural legal constraint. Offshore/foreign-regulated digital EMIs are not licensed by the RBV to take deposits or maintain local IBANs for Vanuatu International Companies, as the RBV licenses credit institutions under the Financial Institutions (Amendment) Act 2020 and prohibits unlicensed deposit-taking. In practice, the entity may use global payment processors (Stripe Billing, Paddle) for SaaS collections, settle those flows into local VUV/USD bank accounts at ANZ or BSP, and employ a foreign EMI strictly as an auxiliary payment-card or FX rail — never as primary treasury custody.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under RBV AML/CFT Directions, customer due diligence requires identification and verification of all directors, authorised signatories, and beneficial owners. Tier-1 banks generally mandate an in-person or supervised videoconference interview with at least one director or the designated authorised signatory at account opening. Remote opening is permitted only where the IC qualifies for reduced CDD (low-risk, standard SaaS profile), all corporate records are apostilled or legalised, and a notarised power of attorney is furnished.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO ambiguity arising from nominee/registered-agent shareholding structures typical of International Companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of beneficial owners under the Companies (Amendment) Act 2017, certified corporate share register, statutory declaration from the Vanuatu-licensed agent, and a legal opinion identifying every natural person with direct or indirect control exceeding 25%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Network/geographic risk due to tax-exempt International Company classification and historical FATF grey-list scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic Substance documentation under the Vanuatu Economic Substance Act 2023, executed commercial contracts with named customers, physical office or operational evidence, utility and telecommunication invoices, and an entity substance memo prepared by a Vanuatu law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsubstantiated source of funds from cross-border SaaS subscription volumes without a coherent invoicing and revenue trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aggregated payment processor statements from Stripe Billing and Paddle, a ledger of customer subscriptions with corresponding invoices, bank statements, and interim or audited financial statements matching SaaS revenue to identifiable customer payment records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or high-risk jurisdiction nexus detected in customer IP addresses, payer geolocation, or counterparty payment routing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented IP-geolocation blocking policy, sanctions screening logs, customer country exclusion list, geolocation evidence confirming prohibited jurisdictions are blocked, and a compliance attestation by the designated AML officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own bank to the Vanuatu IC's capital escrow account at ANZ or BSP, with payment purpose code indicating 'equity capital contribution / direct investment' and the reference 'S001 — Share Capital'. The bank will require the VIPA foreign-investment approval certificate (Foreign Investment Act 1998), a directors' resolution allotting shares under the Companies Act (International Company provisions), and a source-of-funds declaration. Verification is completed through standard KYC documentation plus an independent legal opinion from a Vanuatu-licensed registered agent. No RBV exchange-control permit is required, but the bank will file the transaction with the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit for statistical and AML reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clear rails: local disbursements in VUV via the Vanuatu National Payment System (VANPS) for domestic supplier invoices; cross-border software licensing distributions, contractor payments, and infrastructure fees via SWIFT MT103 over AUD/USD accounts through Australian and New Zealand correspondent corridors; larger or higher-risk disbursements settled via documentary collections or standby/commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600 at the BSP or ANZ trade desks, with presentation through the beneficiary's correspondent bank. Treasury visibility is supported by host-to-host banking APIs where available.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable AUD/USD and AUD/VUV forward contracts executed with ANZ or BSP dealing desks against booked SaaS receipts and disbursement schedules
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/VUV concluded offshore with licensed international banks referencing the RBV-published VUV/AUD fixation
USD/VUV currency swaps with licensed banks for trade-related and intercompany liquidity mismatch under bank-approved derivative limits
FX option collars on USD-denominated subscription inflows via authorised onshore or offshore FX dealers, conditional on bank confirmation of remittance capacity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after every anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of US$200; continued default beyond 6 months may trigger administrative strike-off from the Register and dissolution of the company

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit threshold applies to a Vanuatu International Company unless the company's articles of association require an audit or the VFSC/court directs otherwise
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting framework is prescribed; International Companies commonly maintain books under IFRS or recognised local GAAP for internal management purposes

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vanuatu International Companies are not subject to a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing; however the registered agent must maintain adequate beneficial ownership records under the AML/CFT framework and any shareholding transfer must be recorded promptly in the Register of Members within 30 days of the transfer

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for exempt International Companies; voluntary audit typically US$1,500 - US$3,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Vanuatu International Companies (ICs) are expressly exempt from all corporate income tax, VAT, stamp duty, capital gains tax, and withholding tax on distributions. The exemption is codified under the International Companies Act 1992 (Cap 222). No statutory tax holidays or preferential deduction regime is required because the headline rate is already zero; the tax-exempt status operates as a permanent statutory exemption rather than a time-limited incentive.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Not applicable for Vanuatu International Companies. There is no annual corporate income tax return filing obligation for ICs. The sole periodic filing requirement is the annual return and license fee renewal submitted via the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) electronic portal (VFSC e-services or authorised registered agent).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annually no later than the anniversary of the date of incorporation (i.e., within 30 days before or after the anniversary of registration); the registered agent must submit the annual return and pay the prescribed government license fee to maintain good standing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered exact name of the International Company as per the certificate of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the registered name exactly; a non-resident beneficial owner need not be disclosed on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique VFSC registration number assigned at incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the VFSC registration number; no tax file number exists because the entity is tax-exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address of the registered agent in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a valid Vanuatu registered agent address; cannot be a PO Box only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Licensed VFSC registered agent responsible for the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must use a licensed Vanuatu registered agent; agent details must be current.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of all current directors (information maintained on the confidential register).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors may be non-residents; nominee directors may be used but must be disclosed to the agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of shareholders, if maintained by the agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearers shares are prohibited; beneficial ownership information is confidential but must be held by the registered agent for AML compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Declaration of No Local Business Activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Affirmation that the IC has not carried on business with Vanuatu residents or owned Vanuatu land.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Standard declaration; any local economic activity would jeopardise the international company status and trigger domestic tax exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual government fee based on authorised share capital or flat fee schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee payable via agent; failure to pay triggers strike-off and loss of corporate existence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual return or pay the VFSC license fee by the anniversary date incurs late penalties (typically a fixed late fee plus possible restoration fees), administrative strike-off from the register, and if the company continues trading while struck off, the directors may be personally liable for debts incurred. VFSC also imposes escalating monetary penalties for late annual returns and may suspend the registered agent's authority.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Companies; Vanuatu does not impose any dividend withholding tax on distributions by ICs to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu's tax treaty network is extremely limited. Where a double tax agreement or tax information exchange agreement exists, the entity or payor may apply for treaty relief by obtaining a tax residence certificate from the Vanuatu Ministry of Finance / VFSC. Vanuatu ICs are generally neither Vanuatu tax residents nor eligible for DTA benefits because they are tax-exempt; the protocol for treaty relief is therefore usually inapplicable. In practice, no DTA claim is required because the IC does not pay Vanuatu tax on repatriation, and inbound treaty relief would be determined by the source-country jurisdiction's rules on tax-exempt foreign companies and substance requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding tax in Vanuatu on royalties and interest paid by an International Company to non-residents. Vanuatu has no general withholding tax regime for ICs. Source-country withholding may apply in the jurisdiction of the payee; treaty rates are generally unavailable due to the absence of DTA provisions covering ICs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: VUV 0 / Not applicable. Vanuatu has no domestic transfer pricing legislation, no statutory TP documentation thresholds, and no local file/master file requirement for International Companies. However, to manage source-country transfer pricing risk, a no-code SaaS/website builder entity with cross-border related-party transactions should maintain contemporaneous TP documentation where intercompany charges exceed the destination jurisdiction's filing thresholds (commonly USD 1 million for master file or local file triggers in the counterparty jurisdiction).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu International Companies are subject to limited economic substance expectations only to the extent of maintaining a registered office, registered agent, and adequate records. Vanuatu has not enacted EU-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). For a no-code website builder (ISIC 6201), the substance requirement in any high-tax parent jurisdiction may require actual management, employees, and servers in that jurisdiction. If the IC is treated by a foreign tax authority as a controlled foreign company or shell, it may be subject to CFC tax, economic substance tests, or denial of benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Vanuatu IC as a shell to conceal beneficial ownership from foreign tax authorities, failing to report worldwide income, or falsely claiming the IC is the true economic owner of IP and SaaS revenue while all decisions and employees are located in a high-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Vanuatu International Companies Act 1992 and applicable foreign tax laws, the entity may be struck off or dissolved; criminal fines for false declarations; in foreign courts, the company's tax-exempt status may be disregarded to impose domestic corporate tax, interest, and penalties up to 200% of the understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face civil restitution of unpaid taxes, asset freezes, travel bans, and imprisonment for fraudulent evasion where the corporate veil is pierced as a sham or mere façade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding or licensing high-value intangible property (no-code templates, proprietary code, customer contracts) through the IC without employees, office premises, or board meetings, while all revenue is routed from the operating entity to the IC as deductible fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign anti-avoidance rules (CFC, transfer pricing, substance-based denial) may recharacterise the income as taxable in the shareholder's jurisdiction; penalties for inaccurate transfer pricing documentation typically 25-40% of the adjustment; EU blacklisting consequences may trigger enhanced due diligence and possibly listing of Vanuatu as non-cooperative.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and directors who create artificial arrangements without substance can be assessed jointly and severally for the tax and penalties; director disqualification and travel restrictions may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain adequate records of the beneficial owner, failure to identify high-risk counterparties, processing Stripe/Paddle SaaS payments for anonymous or sanctioned clients, or engaging in money laundering typologies such as invoice circularity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Vanuatu Anti-Money Laundering and Proliferation Financing Act 2020, fines up to VUV 200 million for body corporates and imprisonment up to 15 years for individuals; non-monetary penalties include suspension of the registered agent license and the company's deregistration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face personal criminal liability, civil penalties, and disqualification if knowingly involved in or willfully blind to money laundering, fraud, or terrorist financing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Annual Return and License Fee Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the annual return or pay the VFSC license fee on the anniversary of incorporation for more than three months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalties accumulate from the due date, the company may be struck off the Register of International Companies, and all assets vested in the company escheat to the Crown or VFSC until restoration; restoration fees and court orders may be required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who continue trading after strike-off are personally liable for the company's debts and contractual obligations; directors may be fined or imprisoned under the International Companies Act for providing false statements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC carries on business with Vanuatu residents (other than to obtain professional services), owns or leases real estate in Vanuatu, or provides services to Vanuatu persons, thereby breaching the restrictions applicable to International Companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of international company status and conversion to a domestic Vanuatu company, immediate tax liability on income derived from Vanuatu at the standard rate, monetary penalties for each offending transaction, and potential deregistration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit unauthorised local business activity can be held personally liable for penalties, taxes, and indemnification of the company's losses.
